The data a heatmap layer drew its tiles from, one column per aesthetic

Source: R/ggplot2_heatmap_layer_processor.R
heat_source_frame.Rd

ggplot2 evaluates each aesthetic in the data the layer draws, its own data or else the plot's (Layer$layer_data()), under the layer's mapping and, unless inherit.aes = FALSE, the plot's. So aes(fill = score * 2) draws each tile from twice its score. Each was looked up instead as a column named after its mapping: "score * 2" names none, so every cell was read missing, and an expression for x or y, as factor(month, levels = month.abb), or a layer drawn from data of its own, stopped the reading.

Usage

heat_source_frame(plot, layer_index)

Arguments

plot

The ggplot2 object

layer_index

The layer's index in plot$layers

Value

A list: data, the layer's data with each tile's x, y and fill in the columns .maidr_heat_x, .maidr_heat_y and .maidr_heat_fill; and fill_label, the fill's name as ggplot2 labels it ("score * 2"), or NULL when the fill is not mapped

Details

An x or y the layer does not map is read from the data's first or second column, as it was before, and as missing where the data has no such column. A fill the layer does not map is read as missing: its tiles are all drawn in one colour, so no column of the data is what they show. It was read from the data's third column, whatever that held. An aesthetic that cannot be evaluated against the layer's data, or is no vector there, is read as missing too. An after_stat() of a variable the stat computes names no column of it, as after_stat(group) does, or names a function: after_stat(density) is stats::density() there, which stopped the reading. A fill of categories is read by the numbers its legend shows, as factor(score * 10) shows 10, 20 and 30, and as missing where the names are not numbers, as fill = grade and the colours after_scale() gives: a factor was read as its level codes.
